plan.title: My First Month in the Gym - 30 Days Beginner Guide
plan.note: Same 3-day routine is repeated every week for all 4 weeks. Weights should be moderate, no set should go to failure. Finish each session in 50-70 minutes. Do a warm-up before and dead hang stretch after every session.

exercises.name: Flat Bench Press
cues: Keep a natural arch in your back
Grip wider than shoulders, lower bar close to chest
Slow and steady, no jerking, squeeze the chest

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
cues: Use low incline (about 25 degrees), not high incline
Do not lower dumbbells too deep, it strains the shoulders
Keep both feet flat on the floor

exercises.name: Pec Deck Fly
cues: Adjust seat so shoulders are level with the handles
Keep a slight bend in the elbows
Do not pull handles too far back; squeeze then stretch

exercises.name: Bent Arm Dumbbell Pullover
cues: Lie on the bench with head on it, elbows bent
Lower only to a comfortable chest stretch to avoid shoulder injury
Feel contraction in the chest on the way back

exercises.name: Front Military Press
cues: Grip just outside shoulder width
Press overhead until elbows are straight, move your head under the bar
No jerking, do not lower the bar extremely

exercises.name: Dumbbell Side Lateral Raise
cues: Lift both dumbbells until parallel to the ground
Keep wrist, elbow and shoulder in a straight line
Controlled reps, no jerk

exercises.name: Barbell Upright Row
cues: Grip about 6 inches, inside shoulder width
Pull the bar up close to the chin, bending the elbows
Lift using the traps and squeeze them

exercises.name: Barbell Curl
cues: Shoulder-width grip
Do not swing your back; lift with biceps until you feel the squeeze
Lower fully and let elbows straighten

exercises.name: Alternate Dumbbell Curl
cues: Rotate the dumbbell as you curl up, turn back halfway down
Keep elbows still
Alternate hands while the other arm rests

exercises.name: V-Bar Push Down
cues: Moderate weight, learn the form first
Lean slightly forward from the pelvis
Keep elbows fixed, push down until arms are straight and squeeze triceps

exercises.name: Both Arm Barbell French Press
cues: Grip about 8 inches wide
Lower the bar only to a comfortable stretch
Let elbows move naturally, do not force them inward

exercises.name: Barbell Wrist Curl
cues: Sit on the floor, forearms resting on the bench, wrists hanging off
Grip about 6 inches, inside shoulder width
Curl the wrists up, then stretch down slowly

exercises.name: Leg Raise
cues: Hands under hips, one leg at a time as a beginner
Keep knee soft, lower leg without touching the floor
Engage the abs, slow and steady

exercises.name: Knee High Crunches
cues: Legs in the air with knees bent, hands behind head
Lift only your upper back as far as comfortable
Squeeze at the top for a second, then lower fully

exercises.name: Lat Pull Down
cues: Grip about 28 inches, outside shoulder width
Secure knees under the pad
Pull to upper chest, keep shoulders down, squeeze the back

exercises.name: Mid Row
cues: Retract shoulders and lift chest before pulling
Pull handle to the abs, pause 1 second, squeeze the back
Do not round the back or let shoulders roll forward on release

exercises.name: Barbell Shrugs
cues: Grip outside shoulder width
Lift shoulders as high as comfortable and pause 1 second
Use the traps, connect mind to muscle

exercises.name: Squats
cues: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly outward
Sit back until thighs are parallel to the ground; knees should not go past toes
Chest up, back straight, never fully lock the knees during the set

exercises.name: Leg Press
cues: Feet centered on the platform, toes slightly pointed out
Do not lower so far that hips lift off the pad
Keep knees slightly bent at the top, never lock out

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
cues: Pad sits just above the ankles, knees just off the pad edge
Curl up until hamstrings squeeze
Do not fully straighten the knees, keep tension on the hamstrings

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
cues: Balls of feet on the platform, heels free, knees slightly bent
Rise up on toes until you feel a strong squeeze
Lower heels fully for a good stretch; light hand support is fine

extraSections.title: Dead hang stretch after every workout

beginnerTips.title: Breathing pattern
beginnerTips.summary: Breathe out when you contract the muscle (lifting against gravity), breathe in on the way back.

beginnerTips.title: Muscle pump
beginnerTips.summary: Muscles swell after 3-4 sets. It fades within hours, which is normal. If you never feel it, check diet, sleep and intensity.

beginnerTips.title: Muscle soreness
beginnerTips.summary: Soreness starts about 36 hours after training and can last another 36 hours. It is normal, keep training regularly.

beginnerTips.title: Good pain vs bad pain
beginnerTips.summary: Muscle burn in the last few reps is good pain. Joint pain or extreme pulling is bad pain: stop, ice it, and see a doctor.

beginnerTips.title: Avoid overtraining
beginnerTips.summary: More exercise does not mean more muscle. Keep the whole session between 50 and 70 minutes.

beginnerTips.title: Workout timing
beginnerTips.summary: Any time of day works, but train at the same time every day so your body clock and meals stay consistent.

warmup.title: Warm-Up (do before every workout)
warmup.note: Keep the warm-up short (5-10 min). Finish with 1-2 light ramp-up sets of your first exercise before working sets.

exercises.name: Joint Rotations
exercises.notes: General front and back rotations, clockwise and anti-clockwise.

exercises.name: Toe Touches
exercises.notes: Stretch down to touch your feet with legs slightly apart.

exercises.name: Jumping
exercises.notes: Brief rest between the two sets.

exercises.name: Neck Rotations
exercises.notes: Clockwise and anti-clockwise, keep it slow and gentle.

additionalExercises.name: Leg Swings
additionalExercises.notes: 30 seconds per leg, forward and back

additionalExercises.name: Dynamic Mobility Drills
additionalExercises.notes: 30 seconds, choose moves for the day's muscles
